title: The composition root's own wiring table documents live_vocab as Vocabulary.live_size(), directly contradicting LM.decode's frozen contract -- the exact critical dead-row-masking defect round1 filed would be reintroduced the moment this table is wired up
failure: LM.decode's frozen docstring (lm/api.py:484-488, 516-522) is explicit and detailed: the caller MUST pass `Vocabulary.size()` -- the full positional id count -- as `live_vocab`, specifically NOT `live_size()`, "precisely so that this boundary does not move when a row is retired ... a suffix rule would mask the wrong rows -- and on the probation arms most minted tokens were retired." This is the direct repair for round1's filed critical finding (decode masked live token rows 260-2XX because live_vocab was bound to live_size()). Yet compose.py's own wiring table -- the normative description of what argument each row supplies, read by K10/K11 and meant to be the thing a future implementer of the loop copies verbatim -- states TWICE, in two independent rows, that `live_vocab` comes from a live_size-flavored quantity: the assembly-time 'vocab' row (line 339: "live_vocab -- Vocabulary.live_size under LM.decode's spelling") and the per-flush 'judge_probation' refresh row (line 1098: "live_vocab -- Judgement.live_size under the same consumer's spelling"). Both are asserted as settled fact with no caveat, no TODO and no cross-reference to LM.decode's own docstring, which says the opposite. If the loop driver is written by copying this table -- which is its entire purpose -- every probation-heavy run (the docstring's own example: 217 and 224 of 256 minted tokens retired) reintroduces the exact -inf-on-live-rows failure a second time, at the wiring layer rather than the call-site layer where it was caught and fixed the first time.
evidence: src/lm/api.py:516-519: "`live_vocab` IS THE COUNT OF MINTED ROWS ... the caller passes Vocabulary.size() -- the full id count -- rather than live_size(), precisely so that this boundary does not move when a row is retired." versus src/spine/compose.py:338-339: "live_vocab -- Vocabulary.live_size under LM.decode's spelling;" and src/spine/compose.py:1097-1098 (the judge_probation row): "live_vocab -- Judgement.live_size under the same consumer's spelling." Both compose.py sites name a live_size-derived quantity for the argument LM.decode's own contract says must be the full size.
fix: Correct both compose.py rows to say `live_vocab -- Vocabulary.size() under LM.decode's spelling` (assembly row) and `live_vocab -- vocab.size() (NOT Judgement.live_size) under the same consumer's spelling` (judge_probation row), matching LM.decode's frozen requirement -- and when the loop driver is actually written, assert this at a call site or in a test, since two independently-worded rows agreeing on the wrong quantity is exactly the kind of error a single K-check reading the table cannot catch on its own.
